source.title: Adelie penguin area-wide breeding population census, 1991, present.

ecological_question: Under shared regional marine forcing, do the five historically monitored Palmer Adélie breeding islands decline synchronously, or do island-specific breeding filters produce divergent rates and extinction timing?
why_this_is_island_ecology: All five islands lie in the same local Palmer marine neighborhood and are censused synoptically, reducing large-scale oceanographic differences relative to broad geographic comparisons.
Penguins obtain food at sea, so island-to-island differences primarily represent breeding-patch filters rather than complete terrestrial trophic environments.
The design therefore tests how local island habitat modulates a shared regional forcing.

preprocessing.island_total: sum num_breeding_pairs across all colony_code rows in the annual island census
preprocessing.year: calendar year parsed from ERDDAP time
preprocessing.repeated_dates_within_study_island: allowed only if colony_code rows form one census date; otherwise flag for review

primary_quantities: regional total across the five islands for years with all five islands observed
each island's share of the regional population
fraction remaining relative to its first complete observation
first observed zero following a positive count and whether zero persists
annual finite log growth log(N_t/N_t-1) for consecutive positive observations
pairwise correlation of annual log growth on overlapping years
community synchrony phi = Var(sum island counts)/(sum island temporal SD)^2 on the complete five-island panel

primary_hypotheses.L1_shared_decline: A strong shared regional component should appear as declining total Adélie breeding pairs and positively correlated annual growth across islands.
primary_hypotheses.L2_local_fate_divergence: If island physical filters matter, decline magnitude and local extinction timing should differ substantially among islands despite shared regional forcing.
primary_hypotheses.L3_rank_reordering: Island population ranks and regional population shares should change through time rather than remain fixed under perfectly proportional decline.
primary_hypotheses.L4_extinction_not_simple_scaling: Local extinction should occur earlier on some islands than expected from a uniform multiplicative decline applied to all islands.

local_filter_story_weakened_if: all islands retain nearly constant regional shares
annual changes are almost perfectly synchronous
decline fractions and extinction timing differ little beyond sampling noise

inference_boundaries: This stage does not attribute island differences to snow, geomorphology, competition, or sea ice; those mechanisms are tested only after this descriptive pattern is frozen.
A zero is interpreted as zero breeding pairs in the LTER census, not permanent biological extinction unless subsequent censuses remain zero.
Colony_code changes are not interpreted as colonization/extinction of independent colonies; primary response is island total.
The ERDDAP title says present, but the current exposed time coverage ends in 2017; claims are restricted to the available 1991-2017 panel.
next_stage_if_supported: Freeze and test regional sea-ice versus island-specific snow/geomorphology predictors against annual island deviations from the shared regional trajectory.
